title: I Used the Laser-Cutter Bed Hours on the Mentor Who Left My Honeycomb

parts.text: I stepped into bed two at 2:08 p.m. and mentor Quin was already using my numbered honeycomb. The board said: FORTY MINUTES. HONEYCOMB STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-eight, makerspace steward, holding a clipboard that listed our cut. Quin shrugged. "Mentors keep the bed." I photographed the board, the booking, and his acrylic on my honeycomb. Then I asked for the bed hours. At 2:16 the laser desk pinged why Quin's acrylic sat on our honeycomb. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The laser desk can see Quin's acrylic on bed two during our cut.

social.video_title: He left his acrylic on my numbered honeycomb — Part 1/2
social.description: Laser cutter, a mentor on my honeycomb, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the acrylic. Would you have asked for the bed hours?

parts.text: Quin called it focus tests until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the bed still. The honeycomb went back to my numbered tray. Quin ran a slot of their own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS DO NOT KEEP THE BED. I keep our cut on a labeled card. Quin brown-bags his acrylic. The bed finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Bed hours, numbered honeycomb, and a second line on the board. Were focus tests ever our cut?
